# Measurement map

The function runs on a small set of standing metrics, each with a named owner, a
fixed definition, and — the part that keeps measurement honest — an explicit
statement of what the metric is allowed to justify.

Reach metrics describe distribution and justify distribution decisions only. They
never justify content decisions, because optimizing content for reach is how the
evidence standards erode one reasonable-sounding compromise at a time.

Engagement-quality metrics — replies from practitioners, questions received,
corrections offered — justify content and discovery decisions, and they are read at
the thread level where their meaning lives, not aggregated into a number that hides
which threads carried it.

Outcome metrics — qualified conversations, evaluations started — justify strategy
reviews, and they carry lag disclaimers as part of their definition: an outcome
metric read without its lag window attached is misread by default.

Metric definitions change through the function owner with a dated note in this map,
and dashboards render definitions from the map rather than restating them, so a
definition change cannot silently fork between surfaces. A metric whose definition
cannot be stated in two sentences is retired or split until it can.

## Vanity quarantine

Metrics that measure applause — follower counts, impression totals, award mentions —
live in a labeled vanity section that no decision may cite. They are recorded
because ignoring them entirely invites re-litigating them; they justify nothing
because that is what vanity means here.
